Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:91: However, for the sake of the ways of peace it is permitted to alter [the truth], as explained there in Yevamot (65b), because its attribute unifies everything, as it is said, "and all her paths are peace" (Proverbs 3:17), as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz), and it is the last pillar sustaining the world (Avot 1:17). From this the discerning reader may deduce that one should alter [the truth] for the sake of peace only in a matter that sustains the world, or a matter between a man and his wife, and in the manner of Samuel, who said, "I have come to sacrifice to the Lord" (I Samuel 16:5), which is a matter of saving life.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:92: Likewise, a rectification for one who wishes to repent is that he speak truth — for if he wishes to do something improper, and they say to him, "Did you do such-and-such?" — if he speaks truth, he is forced to say, "Yes, I did it," and he will be ashamed, and the next time he will not do it. Or if they say to him, "Where are you going?" — if he is going to commit a transgression, if he speaks truth he will refrain from doing it because of the shame.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:93: Something one must be careful of, in which many stumble, is with witnesses signing a document — that they should not sign until they have read the document before the borrower and the lender, word by word, and only then sign, so as not to come to testify falsely.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:94: Further, I found an author, among those who speak of matters of piety, in manuscript, speaking well on the matter of truth, and we shall quote his words, please God, in these words: the attribute of truth — the neshamah is created from the place of the holy spirit of the Name, as it is said, "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Genesis 2:7), and it was hewn from the place of purity, and created from the supernal splendor and from the Throne of Glory; and there is no falsehood above, in the place of the Holy of Holies, only truth, as it is said, "but the Lord God is truth" (Jeremiah 10:10); and God made man upright (Ecclesiastes 7:29), to make use of His seal, for the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth (Shabbat 55a), and it is written, "he who speaks falsehoods shall not be established before my eyes" (Psalms 101:7). When a person is occupied with falsehood, then falsehood is not attached to truth. And when there is truth, it is as if His dwelling in heaven is established in regard to people, for when there is truth among people, they acknowledge that He made heaven and earth and the sea and everything — this is [the meaning of] "who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them" (Psalms 146:6), and adjacent to it, "who keeps truth forever"; and when there is falsehood among people, it is as if there is no place for His dwelling in heaven and earth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:95: Whoever merits to reflect on these matters, his neshamah is hewn from the place of truth, and he will do all his affairs in truth, and not introduce falsehood into the place of holiness and truth. Therefore it is said, "the Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth" (Psalms 145:18) — and what is called a "true calling"? This is one who empties his heart of every worldly matter and draws near to the Name alone, and his intellect goes on strengthening itself to cleave to the supernal light, and sets his thought always on his yearning. This matter a person attains when he secludes himself in his chamber; therefore every pious person should increase seclusion and separation, and not associate with anyone except for great necessity. But if he prays while moving his lips, and turns his face to the wall, yet you are thinking of your own affairs and needs, and reciting with your tongue about your household matters — or to be honored, thinking in your heart, "How pleasant is my voice!" and striving in your prayer to find favor in people's eyes to receive praise from them — this, your service is not true. Therefore we pray, "and purify our hearts to serve You in truth," that all our service be done in truthfulness, with belief, with a whole heart and a willing soul, and not for the sake of people, and not for money or for vain distraction.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:96: This is what King David, peace be upon him, said: "Lord, who shall sojourn in Your tabernacle, who shall dwell in Your holy mountain? He who walks uprightly, and works righteousness, and speaks truth in his heart" (Psalms 15:1-2). Consider what it says, "and speaks truth in his heart," and does not say "speaks truth with his mouth" — rather, the intent is that truth should be fixed and established both among people and in his heart. Therefore the early pious ones, when they had a purchase or sale, would give it to the buyer according to what they had agreed in their hearts to sell it for, even if the buyer wished to add more, they would take only according to what they had agreed in their hearts. An important person walking this path of speaking truth in his heart, if he undertook in his mind to do a certain thing, should write down that intention so as not to forget it and not deviate from any part of his intention; and if he cannot stand by it, he should go to a sage and have him annul the intentions he decided in his heart, even though he did not utter them from his mouth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:97: Whoever speaks truth in his heart and does not wish to speak falsehood — even matters he thinks and speaks without intending them to be binding, nevertheless his words are fulfilled, as it is said, "you shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you" (Job 22:28). And whoever is a man of truth in all his dealings, whether in buying and selling or in lending, should always say at the first instance his final intention, and accustom those who deal with him to know that he will not change his words, neither adding nor subtracting.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:98: The sage said: always set truth before you — meaning, he should make a sign for himself when he comes to conduct business, so that he remembers and does not speak falsehood; and he should write it down and bring it with him and look at it before his dealings; and likewise write it in his study hall and on his table, that he remember and not speak falsehood, so that it not be forgotten and he not fail to know a true matter. And so a certain sage did — he wrote on the walls above, "Remember the day of your death and do not sin."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:99: Whoever speaks nothing but truth shall live and lengthen his days and be saved from all evil, as proven from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, when he leaped [into Paradise while still alive], and so on — for the Angel of Death did not rule over him during his life, since he never in his life spoke any falsehood or lie, and he is still in the Garden of Eden in his lifetime (Ketubot 77b); support for this is what the verse says, "but the Lord God is truth, He is the living God and the everlasting King" (Jeremiah 10:10). And if he speaks nothing but truth, he will be saved all his days from all evil, as it is written, "the Torah of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found on his lips; he walked with Me in peace and uprightness... for he is the messenger of the Lord of Hosts" (Malachi 2:6-7) — for the supernal angels are forms of truth and are not in bodies, and souls are hewn from them like light, and souls are like bodies; therefore they know hidden things only a little, and in a nighttime vision when the soul is not occupied with the body's needs. And one who knows the mystery of the soul will testify to the matter — that dreams are a kind of thought, "your thoughts came into your mind upon your bed" (Daniel 2:29), and dreams come through the angel who accompanies people; and since not all thoughts are true, not all dreams are true. And whoever trains himself so that all his thoughts are true will also see true visions at night and know the future, like the angels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:100: There is no virtue greater than one who speaks truth; therefore, "the sum of Your word is truth" (Psalms 119:160), and he warned, "keep far from a false matter" (Exodus 23:7). Also, a person's hints [implicit statements] should be true, for the reward of truth is very great. Therefore let a person train himself to walk in truth, and study Torah so that he knows truth, and so that he can fulfill the commandments in their truth and according to their halachah, and always acknowledge the truth — and even in matters of Aggadah, which involve no fulfillment of a commandment, he should study, so that his heart believes a true matter. Do not be ashamed to accept the truth from whatever place it comes — even from the least of the least and the most despised of the despised, accept the truth from him — for a fine pearl in the hand of a small, despised person is still valuable as a pearl.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:101: Now, because of our sins, since the exile has lasted too long, Israel must separate from the vanities of the world and hold fast to the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is truth, and sanctify themselves even in what is permitted to them, and not lie either to a Jew or to a gentile, nor deceive him in any matter, as it is said, "the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth" (Zephaniah 3:13), and it is written, "and I will sow her for Myself in the land" (Hosea 2:25) — does a person sow a single kor and not find several kors? So the Holy One, blessed be He, sows Israel among the nations so that converts might be added to them (Pesachim 87b); but as long as they conduct themselves with deception, who would attach themselves to them? Behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, was strict regarding the robbery of the wicked, as it is said, "and the earth was filled with violence" (Genesis 6:11).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:102: There was a story of Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach, who bought a donkey from an Ishmaelite; his students went and found a precious stone hanging on its neck, and brought the stone to Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach and said to him, "This is the Lord's blessing that will enrich you." He said to them, "I bought a donkey, I did not buy a precious stone," and he returned it to that Ishmaelite; and that Ishmaelite called out, "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach" (Devarim Rabbah 3:3). And so it is in the Yerushalmi (Bava Metzia 2:5), that the early sages bought wheat from gentiles and found in it a purse of money, and returned it to them, and the gentiles opened it and said, "Blessed is the Lord, the God of the Jews." And there are many similar stories warning of the sanctification of the Name, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:103: When there is truth below, then the Name looks down with righteousness upon the earth, as it is said, "truth shall spring from the earth, and righteousness shall look down from heaven" (Psalms 85:12). Therefore hold fast to truth, whether the matter is evil or good — do not abandon the truth, and rely on the Faithful One, as it is written, "and you shall know that the Lord your God... is the faithful God, who keeps covenant and mercy..." (Deuteronomy 7:9). What is His faithfulness in keeping the covenant? If there is a righteous person who has sinned, He exacts his recompense in this world. And this is a clear matter: it is better for the righteous to be judged even with the sufferings of Job in his body all his days, which is a despicable thing, and for a short time while he is in this world, and to have his good recompense given in the honored matter in the supernal world, attaining supernal levels in the good time that is entirely long and never ceases — this is better for the righteous than being whole in this world and not paying for his sins in this world, and being judged in the World to Come with the sufferings of Gehinnom, or, because of his sin, having his neshamah diminished from its level in the world of souls, attached to the splendor of the supernal levels, for which pleasure there is no comparison or likeness. To the wicked, they give their recompense in a small, ceasing pleasure, in the short world, which is this world, while their sin is reserved for the long world, with great suffering — that is, Gehinnom — for which suffering there is no comparison; and the verse is explicit, "and repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them" (Deuteronomy 7:10) — meaning, the Holy One, blessed be He, repays the wicked person's merits in this world in order to destroy him for the World to Come. Further it says, "He will not delay him who hates Him; He will repay him to his face" — this is said regarding a righteous person, that He repays him for his sins in this world so that he may have the World to Come. May the Merciful One guide us in His truth, and bring us into His chambers, to reach the light where His hidden might and the beauty of His glory dwell — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:104: And with this the chapter is concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:1: Regarding the punishment of the class of tellers of evil speech, and its divisions — and because this discourse is longer, we saw fit to dedicate it a chapter of its own. It says in the Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Metzora 1): three kings and four commoners have no share in the World to Come — the four commoners are Balaam, Doeg, Achitophel, and Gehazi; you find that these were pushed into Gehinnom because of the speech of their mouths — and it brings proof for each one; but to avoid being lengthy, we shall not quote their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:2: Further, there: Rabbi Pedat said, a covenant has been made by the Holy One, blessed be He, with the world, that whoever tells evil speech will be stricken with tzara'at — from where? From the fact that they called this passage "this shall be the law of the metzora (leper)" — the law of one who spreads a bad name (motzi shem ra). Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, plagues come upon a person only because of the evil speech he utters from his mouth; and the holy spirit cries out and says, "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin" (Ecclesiastes 5:5) — do not cause your body to be stricken; "and do not say before the angel, it was an error" — do not say before the one appointed over you [that] the speech was inadvertent, for every single utterance that comes from your mouth is written in a book, whether good or evil, whether inadvertent or deliberate. And from where do we know this is so? As it is said, "then those who feared the Lord spoke to one another, and the Lord listened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him, for those who feared the Lord and thought upon His Name" (Malachi 3:16). And likewise regarding the attribute of retribution, David said, "You know my sitting down and my rising up, You understand my thought from afar" (Psalms 139:2), and Job said, "for now You number my steps" (Job 14:16), "You set a print upon the heels of my feet" (Job 13:27) — "Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?" — these are the hands and the body that are stricken with tzara'at.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:3: And in Eleh HaDevarim Rabbah (Parashat Ki Tetze), it explains this verse, "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin," as expounded; however, regarding the end of the verse, "and do not say before the angel [that it was an error]" — they, of blessed memory, said [this means]: do not say, "I will go and speak evil speech and no creature will know"; the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "Know that I send an angel who stands beside you and writes down everything you speak about your fellow." From where? As it is said, "do not curse the king, even in your thought" (Ecclesiastes 10:20) — why? "For a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" — and what is "and that which has wings shall tell the matter"? These are the angels of whom it is written, "each had six wings" (Isaiah 6:2) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:4: The pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, wrote, in the Mishnah "whoever desecrates the Name of Heaven in secret" (Avot 4:4), regarding evil speech, a fitting matter, together with this passage explaining the verse "and do not say before the angel that it was an error," [teaching] that every single utterance is written — I have seen fit to quote it here, in these words: it seems to me that included in "whoever desecrates the Name of Heaven in secret" is one who tells evil speech, because there is found on his wings the dust of three severe transgressions, whose root, in each case, requires one to be killed rather than transgress, as they said, of blessed memory (Arachin 15b). Regarding idolatry it is written, "Alas, this people has sinned a great sin" (Exodus 32:31); regarding forbidden relations, "how then can I do this great wickedness" (Genesis 39:9); regarding bloodshed it is written, "my iniquity is greater than can be borne" (Genesis 4:13); and regarding evil speech it is written, "a tongue that speaks great things" (Psalms 12:4).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:5: Do not think he said this by way of exaggeration, but as a matter of true precision — for the idol worshipers used to say, "the Lord does not see us," and therefore they were drawn after those forms of worship to find favor in the eyes of the deities, according to their corrupt understanding. Now, one who tells evil speech about his fellow, when he hears the sound of his footsteps, falls silent and changes his speech, and when he passes from his presence, returns to his corruption, and does not think about the One whose glory fills the whole earth, "His eyes are in every place, watching the evil and the good" (Proverbs 15:3). And the adulterous woman, "she eats, and wipes her mouth, and says, I have done no wrong" (Proverbs 30:20); and one who tells evil speech shows a pleasant face to his fellow before him, but sets his ambush within, and when passing him, mocks him and makes him trampled under the sword of his tongue. Bloodshed needs no explanation, for it is its very foundation — all the more so if he shames him publicly. Since this is so, there is no desecration of the Name greater than this, and therefore they are punished publicly, as it is said, "and the people did not journey until Miriam was gathered in" (Numbers 12:15) — for all knew the greatness of evil speech, even though it was in secret and inadvertent — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:6: It is explained in the Midrash (Yalkut Tehillim, remez 971), on the psalm "When the Ziphites came" (Psalm 54), that concerning one who speaks evil speech it is said, "cursed is he who strikes his fellow in secret" (Deuteronomy 27:24). And so in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer (ch. 52), in these words: whoever informs against a person in secret has no share in the World to Come, as it is said, "whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him will I destroy" (Psalms 101:5), and another verse says, "cursed is he who strikes his fellow in secret." Know that this is so: come and see from the serpent, who informed against Adam and his helper — the Holy One, blessed be He, cursed him that his food be dust, as it is said, "and dust shall you eat all the days of your life" (Genesis 3:14). Rabban Gamliel says, Israel spoke evil speech against the Holy One, blessed be He, saying, "Does the Lord have the power to feed us in the desert?" as it is said, "and they spoke against God, saying, Can God furnish a table in the wilderness? Behold, He struck the rock, so that the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed" (Psalms 78:19-20). And the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that they had spoken slanderously against His glory, and His glory is a consuming fire, and He sent fire and it consumed them at the edge, as it is said, "and the fire of the Lord burned among them, and consumed those in the outer part of the camp" (Numbers 11:1). Israel went to Moses and said to him, "Moses our teacher, would that you had made us like sheep to the slaughter and not to consuming fire!" Moses saw the distress of Israel and prayed — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:7: From this passage you can clearly see that the sin of evil speech blemishes the Shechinah, called His glory, and His glory is a consuming fire — this being "righteousness that has no leniency at all" (Zohar Parashat Balak 199a), and this is the "angel" of whom it is said, "do not say before the angel that it was an error" — for even inadvertently, it punishes, because it is absolute judgment. This is also [the meaning of] "this shall be the law of the metzora" (Leviticus 14:2), which is explained in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Metzora) to be a sword taking vengeance on people whose sword is in their tongue, and she is called "Zot" (this), based on the verse, "be afraid for yourselves of the sword" (Job 19:29). They said, of blessed memory: come and see, through the evil speech that the serpent spoke to the woman, he caused a decree of death to be issued against her, against Adam, and against the whole world; regarding evil speech it is written, "and their tongue a sharp sword" (Psalms 57:5). Therefore, "be afraid for yourselves of the sword" — of evil speech — "for wrath brings the punishments of the sword" — what is "for wrath brings the punishments of the sword"? This is the sword of the Lord, for we have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, has a sword by which He judges the wicked — this is what is written, "the sword of the Lord is filled with blood" (Isaiah 34:6), "and my sword shall devour flesh" (Deuteronomy 32:42), and therefore, "be afraid for yourselves of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword." "That you may know that there is judgment" — so that you know that thus is one judged who has a sword in his tongue: a sword is prepared for him that destroys everything — this is what is written, "this shall be the law of the metzora" — so far his words. And above this it says "that you may know that there is judgment," and it is written [homiletically as] "that they judge him" — the intent being that he is judged by the supernal sword, which is the attribute of "Zot."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:8: Through what is explained — that one who speaks evil speech blemishes the Shechinah — a certain verse in Psalms can be understood, which says, "Woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech..." (Psalms 120:5), and above this it speaks of the matter of evil speech, "What shall be given to you, and what more shall be done to you, you deceitful tongue?" (Psalms 120:3), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain this matter regarding the master of evil speech (Midrash Tehillim on the verse). And the verse following proves this: "Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of broom" (120:4), which is explained to mean that the arrows of the mighty man are, in his evil speech, sharp, as King David, peace be upon him, said of Doeg, "Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man?" (Psalms 52:3), and "whose tongue is sharpened like a sword; they aim their arrow, a bitter word" (Psalms 64:4). "With coals of broom" — Rashi explains, in these words: all coals are extinguished from the outside, [but] these are extinguished from the inside, and they are extinguished from the outside but not from the inside — so far his words. The meaning is that evil speech is like coals of broom that are not extinguished from within — evil speech goes on burning little by little, while extinguished on the outside, since he deceives his fellow and speaks peace to him while setting his ambush within — this being "the deceitful tongue" mentioned above in the verse. The Shechinah complains about this and says, "Woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech" — meaning, he causes, through his sin, the exile to be prolonged, and causes the Shechinah to dwell with the "tents of Kedar," which are the kelipot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:9: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Parashat Acharei Mot 75b), whose wording we quoted in the Gate of Awe, please God (ch. 5), that Israel is delayed in exile because of three matters — because they demean the Shechinah, and so on — and all of them are found in one who speaks evil speech, since the nakedness of speech is more repugnant than everything, and they turn their faces from the Shechinah, in the manner explained by the pious author, peace be upon him, whose wording we quoted above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:10: Further, another explanation is offered in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 16:5), on the verse mentioned (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth," in these words: "do not let your mouth" — this refers to Miriam, "and Miriam spoke" (Numbers 12:1). "Cause your flesh to sin" — do not give permission to one of your limbs to cause all your limbs to sin. "And do not say before the angel" — this refers to Moses, as it is written, "and He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt" (Numbers 20:16). "That it was an error" — "we have done foolishly and we have sinned" (Numbers 12:11). "Why should God be angry at your voice" — "and the anger of the Lord was kindled against them, and He departed" (Numbers 12:9). "And destroy the work of your hands" — she sinned with her mouth, and all the other limbs were stricken, as it is written, "and the cloud departed from over the tent..." (Numbers 12:10) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:11: Further on: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, five "laws" are written in this passage: "this is the law of the tzara'at plague" (Leviticus 13:59), "this is the law for all manner of tzara'at plague" (14:55), "this shall be the law of the metzora" (14:2), "this is the law of him in whom is the tzara'at plague" (14:32), "this is the law of tzara'at" (14:57) — "one who spreads a bad name" — to teach you that whoever speaks evil speech transgresses five books of the Torah; therefore Moses warns Israel — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:12: Further, in Midrash Tanchuma (Metzora 2): "this shall be the law of the metzora" — this is what the verse says, "death and life are in the hand of the tongue" (Proverbs 18:21) — everything depends on the tongue: if he merits, [it is] to life; if he causes himself liability, [it is] to death. If a person occupies himself with Torah with his tongue, he merits life, for Torah is a tree of life, as it is said, "she is a tree of life to those who hold fast to her" (Proverbs 3:18), and it is the remedy for evil speech, as it is said, "a healing tongue is a tree of life, but perverseness in it is a wound to the spirit" (Proverbs 15:4). But if a person occupies himself with evil speech, he becomes liable for his soul unto death, for evil speech is worse than bloodshed — for whoever kills, kills only one soul, but whoever tells evil speech kills three: the speaker, the one who accepts it, and the one spoken about. For Doeg spoke evil speech about Achimelech son of Achitub and was killed, as it is said, "and the king said, You shall surely die, Achimelech" (I Samuel 22:16), and Saul was killed, as it is said, "so Saul died for his trespass which he committed against the Lord" (I Chronicles 10:13), and so Saul says, "stand over me and slay me, for anguish (shevatz) has seized me" (II Samuel 1:9) — this being the accusation of Nob, the city of priests, and "shevatz" refers only to the priestly garments, as it is said, "and you shall make settings (mishbetzot) of gold" (Exodus 28:13). And Doeg was uprooted from the life of this world and the life of the World to Come, as it is said, "God shall likewise destroy you forever, He shall take you away, and pluck you out of your dwelling place, and root you out of the land of the living, Selah" (Psalms 52:7) — [being uprooted] from the life of the World to Come. And in the Yerushalmi (Pe'ah 1:1) it says, in the days of Saul three [informers/accomplices] are mentioned, [along with] Abner son of Ner, who had the ability to protest but did not protest. Which is worse, one who strikes with a sword or one who strikes with an arrow? Say: one who strikes with an arrow — for one who strikes with a sword cannot kill his fellow unless he is close to him and touches him, but one who strikes with an arrow is not so, but throws the arrow and strikes him wherever he sees him. Therefore the teller of evil speech is likened to an arrow, as it is said, "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" (Jeremiah 9:7); and so it is said, "the sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword" (Psalms 57:5).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:13: In Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, found in our possession in manuscript, they said, of blessed memory: this is what the verse says, "you shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue..." (Job 5:21) — because evil speech is worse than a sword: one who has a sword in his hand and wishes to kill his fellow, if he wishes to retract, he can, since it is still in his possession; but one who wishes to kill his fellow with an arrow, once the arrow has left his hand, cannot retract, for the arrow has already left his hand. Likewise, one who speaks evil speech about his fellow cannot retract it, and so the verse testifies concerning them, "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" — so far his words, as pertains to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:14: Further, in Midrash Tanchuma, in the chapter mentioned, in these words: another interpretation, "death and life are in the hand of the tongue" — evil speech is harsh, for a person does not utter it from his mouth without denying the fundamental principle [of faith], as it is said, "who have said, With our tongue we shall prevail, our lips are with us, who is master over us?" (Psalms 12:5). As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, cries out against tellers of evil speech, "Who shall rise up for me against the evildoers?" (Psalms 94:16) — who can stand against them in Gehinnom? And Gehinnom cries out, "I too cannot stand against them!" He says to it, "I from above and you from below," as it is said, "sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of broom" (Psalms 120:4). The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, "Do you wish to escape from Gehinnom? Distance yourselves from evil speech, and you will merit this world and the World to Come," as it is said, "Who is the man who desires life..." and it is written, "guard your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit," and it is written, "turn from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it." Therefore it is said, "this shall be the law of the metzora" — "one who spreads a bad name" [read as] "motzi ra" ("who brings forth evil") — for evil plagues are found on his body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:15: See what is written regarding Miriam: "and Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses" (Numbers 12:1); therefore, "and Aaron turned toward Miriam, and behold, she was leprous" (Numbers 12:10). What is written there [elsewhere]? "Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam" (Deuteronomy 24:9). And is this not an a fortiori argument? If Miriam, who spoke only about her brother, and intended only to restore him to his wife, was punished thus — one who speaks evil speech about his fellow, all the more so! What is written above this passage? "Take heed in the plague of tzara'at, to observe diligently" (Deuteronomy 24:8).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:16: And even Aaron, who was High Priest, was touched by the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "and the anger of the Lord was kindled against them, and He departed" (Numbers 12:9) — "against them" [being] against Miriam and Aaron — except that Aaron was healed immediately, and Miriam only after seven days. Therefore, "this shall be the law of the metzora" — "one who spreads a bad name (motzi shem ra)" — one who found evil (matza ra).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:17: And so you find with the primordial serpent, that because he spoke evil speech against his Creator, he was therefore stricken with tzara'at. What did he say? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: [regarding] "for on the day you eat of it your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be like gods, knowing good and evil" (Genesis 3:5) — he said to them, every craftsman hates his fellow craftsman, and when He wished to create His world, He ate from this tree and created His world; you too, if you eat from it, you will be able to create a world like His. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "You have spoken evil speech; you shall eventually be stricken with tzara'at," as it is said, "and the Lord God said to the serpent, Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle" (Genesis 3:14) — with what? With tzara'at, as it is said, "for it is a malignant tzara'at" (Leviticus 13:52). Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Levi: the scaly patches on the serpent are its tzara'at. And not only that, but all those with blemishes are healed in the World to Come, and the serpent is not healed, as it is said, "cursed are you above all cattle" — from here we learn that all are healed, but it is not healed. Regarding people it is written, "then shall the lame man leap as a hart" (Isaiah 35:6), and "then the eyes of the blind shall be opened" (Isaiah 35:5); and likewise the beast and the animal, "the wolf and the lamb shall feed together... and the lion shall eat straw like the ox" (Isaiah 65:25); but the serpent's bread is dust, for it is never healed — since it brought people down to dust, who caused this to it? Because it spoke evil speech — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:18: In the Sifrei it says, in Parashat "and Miriam spoke," an a fortiori argument: if Miriam, who did not intend to speak disparagingly about her brother but rather in praise, not to diminish fruitfulness and multiplication but to increase it, [speaking] about her younger brother, and between herself and him, as it is said, "and He heard..." (Numbers 12:2), was punished thus — one who intends to speak disparagingly about his fellow and not in praise, to diminish fruitfulness and multiplication rather than increase it, about one greater than himself, and before others — all the more so! And further, an a fortiori argument: if King Uzziah, who did not intend to take greatness for himself for his own honor, but for the honor of the Omnipresent, was punished thus — one who intends to take greatness for himself for his own honor, all the more so! — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:19: And in Yalkut (Parashat Devarim, remez 788), on "and Chatzerot" (Deuteronomy 1:1), this passage regarding Miriam is explained further, in these words: "and Chatzerot" — He said to them, should you not have learned from what I did to Miriam in Chazerot? If I did not show favor to Miriam the righteous, an a fortiori argument for the rest of people! If Miriam, who spoke only about her brother, who was younger than her, was punished thus — one who speaks about someone greater than himself, all the more so! Another interpretation: if Miriam, when she spoke, was heard by no creature except the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, as in the matter of "and the Lord heard," was punished thus — one who speaks disparagingly of his fellow before many people, all the more so! — so far his words. And it says "another interpretation," not combining them into one, as in the previous Sifrei passage, to teach us that whichever of these aspects occurs in reality — such as a wise, righteous person who wishes to speak evil speech about someone lesser than himself, or one who speaks it between himself and his fellow with no creature hearing — each and every aspect has its own punishment for evil speech.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:20: In the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 17:3) it further says that plagues come for ten things: for idolatry, for forbidden relations, for bloodshed, for desecration of the Name, for cursing the Name, for robbing the public, for stealing what is not one's own, for haughtiness of spirit, for tellers of evil speech, and for an evil eye — and it derives all of these from verses. In Midrash Tanchuma (Metzora 4) they are brought too, except with some variation between them, which does not pertain to our subject, so we have not quoted its wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:21: In the Zohar (Parashat Balak 206a) it says that plagues come for eleven things, in these words: for idolatry, for cursing the Name, for forbidden relations, for theft, for evil speech, for false testimony, for a judge who corrupts judgment, for a false oath, for one who enters within his fellow's boundary, for one who devises evil thoughts, and for one who sows discord between brothers; and some say also for an evil eye — so far his words; and it derives all of these from proofs — see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:22: In Pesachim (118a) they say, of blessed memory: Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah, whoever tells evil speech, whoever accepts evil speech, and whoever testifies falsely against his fellow deserves to be thrown to the dogs, as it is said, "you shall cast it to the dogs" (Exodus 22:30), and it is written after it, "you shall not accept a false report" (Exodus 23:1), read as "you shall not cause [others] to accept [a false report]" — so far his words. In tractate Arachin (16a) they count only seven — this requires further study.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:23: Further, there in the aforementioned tractate, aforementioned chapter (15b), it says regarding the punishment for evil speech: Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva, whoever tells evil speech deserves to be stoned with a stone — it is written here, "him will I destroy (atzmit)" (Psalms 101:5), and it is written there, "they have cut off (tzamtu) my life in the pit, and cast a stone at me" (Lamentations 3:53). And when you recall what is explained in the Tikkunim (59b, Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 110a) and Ra'aya Meheimna regarding stoning, you will know to what extent the blemish and power of evil speech reaches.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:24: Further, there: Reish Lakish said, whoever tells evil speech magnifies his sins up to the heavens, as it is said, "they set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth" (Psalms 73:9). His intent is regarding the attribute called "Shamayim" (heavens), as they say in the Bahir (item 100), "and You will hear the heavens" (I Kings 8:32) — for it is known that he blemishes "the earth" of the living, as explained above, and it teaches us that the blemish also ascends to "the heavens."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:25: Further, there, Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, what is the remedy for tellers of evil speech? If he is a Torah scholar, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it is said, "a healing tongue is a tree of life" (Proverbs 15:4), and "tongue" refers only to evil speech, as it is said, "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" (Jeremiah 9:7), and "tree of life" refers only to Torah, as it is said, "she is a tree of life to those who hold fast to her" (Proverbs 3:18). And if he is an am ha'aretz (unlearned person), let him lower his mind, as it is said, "but perverseness in it (the tongue) is a wound (shever) to the spirit." Rabbi Abba bar Chanina said, one who tells [evil speech] has no remedy, for David already cut them off with the holy spirit, as it is said, "may the Lord cut off all flattering lips" (Psalms 12:4).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:26: The passage of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina, which gives a remedy for evil speech through Torah and through humility of spirit, certainly has reasoning and is a plausible teaching, for Torah is more valuable than all offerings — for even the sin of desecration of the Name, in the passage regarding the house of Eli (I Samuel 3:14), "the iniquity of the house of Eli shall not be atoned for with sacrifice or offering forever," our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Rosh Hashanah 18a): with sacrifice and offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through words of Torah, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim 80b). Likewise humility is equal to all the offerings, as it is said, "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit" (Psalms 51:19), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Sotah 5b) regarding humility — that it is accounted to him as though he had offered all the offerings. If so, since this one lowers his spirit and his pride, he will be atoned — for the sin of evil speech comes because of pride and insolence, and therefore he does not consider other people to be anything, and speaks whatever comes to his mouth; therefore his remedy is through lowliness, measure for measure.
